claim: superseded() compares created_at as a STRING, and created_at is written with a plain datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() which omits microseconds when they are zero. That orders correctly ONLY because '+' (0x2B) sorts before '.' (0x2E), so a whole second precedes its own fractions. Normalising the offset to 'Z' (0x5A) would silently invert same-second ordering and a resumed delete would supersede an earlier operation
status: DOCUMENTED AND PINNED, not changed. Changing the stored timestamp format is a migration. The dependency is now stated at superseded() where the next reader meets it, and tests/unit/test_write_log_timestamp_ordering.py fails if it stops holding -- including a test asserting a Z-formatted timestamp would break it. pending_write_store._stamp pins timespec='microseconds' for this exact reason; this store relied on the coincidence
